episodes.title: MacroVoices #544 Viktor Shvets: How Markets Survive Disruption
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
MacroVoices interviews Macquarie global strategist Viktor Shvets on Fed independence under new chair Kevin Warsh, the disinflation-vs-stagflation debate, Iran war fallout on oil and gold, record global polarization, AI's "rolling bubble" dynamics, and China's strength/imbalances. The trading desk segment covers COT positioning across S&P 500, DXY, crude and gold plus a major yen intervention — all directly relevant to EM carry and risk appetite.

**Key points**
- Warsh confirmed as Fed chair; Supreme Court carved a unique exception for Fed independence while emasculating other federal agencies.
- Shvets still expects long-run disinflation (tech-driven) but tariffs/immigration/geopolitics create repeated inflation "spikes"; core PCE would be near 2% without these shocks.
- Fed funds at 3.5% is consistent with either near-zero real neutral rates (Miran) or the Fed's own ~1-1.5% estimate once inflation is added.
- Iran war likened to Vietnam (no exit); Russia-Ukraine likened to Korea, could resolve within a year with Ukraine EU-integrated.
- Gold fell over 25% during the Iran conflict as investors favored USD/Treasuries for liquidity; Shvets still sees gold as the ultimate long-term hedge.
- Global polarization (V-Dem index) at record highs: US 2.3, Turkey 3.4, UK/Germany/France/Poland rising; Japan/Australia/Canada least polarized.
- China dominates electrification/robotics/AI but is trapped by a 45% savings rate, misallocating ~$11-12tn/year, unable to pivot to consumption.
- Trading desk: SPX call volume hit a record 4mn contracts; DXY testing key 99.5 support post-FOMC; USDJPY intervention pushed yen from 163 to 158; crude gave back gains toward $75; gold broke out 4% toward 4550 resistance.

**FX / rates implications**
- DXY at an inflection near 99.5 support; a break lower reopens a 15-month range and broad USD weakness, supportive for EM Asia and LATAM carry (INR, IDR, MXN, BRL).
- Record JPY shorts unwinding after coordinated intervention risks a self-reinforcing rally that could spill into broader carry-trade de-risking, a key funding risk for high-yield EM FX.
- Warsh's push for less Fed communication raises rate-path uncertainty, typically lifting EM FX vol and risk premia.
- Oil retreat toward $75 on Iran ceasefire hopes eases EM inflation/import bills (India, Philippines especially), though Aramco flags an 18-month inventory rebuild as a structural floor.
- Gold's broad-based breakout across silver/copper/uranium signals rotation into hard assets, often paralleling EM reserve-diversification flows.
- China's stalled consumption pivot keeps exporting deflation, pressuring regional Asia FX competitiveness (CNY, KRW, TWD).

**Watch list**
- DXY 99.5 support level; gold 4550 Fibonacci resistance.
- This week's COT report for first read on JPY short-covering post-intervention.
- NASDAQ 100 resistance at 30,000/31,000.
- Iran ceasefire talks/Strait of Hormuz status; Russia-Ukraine negotiations.
- Fed communication shifts under Warsh over the next 6-12 months.

episodes.title: Weak Jobs Report, AI Model Fears, and the Data Center Economy 8/7/26
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
A weak US jobs report (-23,000) and an escalating White House effort to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook dominate the macro conversation, alongside a surging gold and copper rally tied to a "currency debasement" trade. For an EM trader, Fed independence risk and the trajectory of rate-cut/hike odds are the key transmission channels into DXY, UST yields and EM carry.

**Key points**
- US payrolls fell 23,000 in the last month; losses concentrated in leisure (post-World Cup) and local government, seen as possible one-offs; labor force participation at a five-year low as both labor supply (immigration curbs) and demand soften.
- White House sent Fed Governor Lisa Cook a letter alleging mortgage fraud and giving her three weeks to respond, reviving the removal effort the Supreme Court previously blocked on procedural grounds; her counsel vows to challenge it.
- Odds of a Fed rate hike this year are falling; Wells Fargo's strategist said the market is coming around to "no hike in 2026," which is bullish for gold.
- Gold up 5% this week (best week since January) on debasement trade, yen intervention and prior Iran-war oil spike; copper hit an all-time high on tariff anticipation (possible 15% tariff on refined copper cathodes) and AI/defense/electrification demand, up 50% year-to-date.
- OpenAI paused rollout of its new Astra model citing critical cyber capability risk, fueling a cybersecurity-stock rally (Palo Alto, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Okta).

**FX / rates implications**
- Fed credibility concerns from politicized removal attempts are framed as ultimately dollar-negative and bond-negative ("bond market says pay me" — higher term premium), a theme relevant to broad DXY direction and EM carry trades.
- Falling US rate-hike odds and a debasement narrative are gold-positive and could pressure USD broadly, a tailwind for EM Asia and LATAM FX if it persists.
- Copper's tariff-driven rally (potential 15% levy on refined cathodes) is a China-demand and industrial-metals signal relevant to commodity-linked LATAM currencies (CLP, PEN).

**Watch list**
- Lisa Cook's three-week response deadline to the White House removal letter; any Supreme Court challenge.
- September FOMC meeting and incoming inflation data as the key swing factor for hike/no-hike odds.
- Commerce Department decision on the 15% tariff on refined copper cathodes.
- President Trump's mining roundtable and any new government stakes in metals/rare-earth companies.
